## Context
This is a log of fixes to bring [alineR](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/alineR/index.html) back to CRAN. Last check from CRAN is [here](http://cran-archive.r-project.org/web/checks/2021/2021-04-21_check_results_alineR.html). We used Claude Opus 5.5 for debugging and fixing, with manual validation of reproducibility and CRAN package checks.

## alineR Replay and Debugging Log
Install archived package 
```R
install.packages("~/Documents/alineR/alineR_archive/alineR_1.1.4.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
library(alineR)
```

Confirm we can reproduce previous results
```R
aline("kərampu", "ləməntuŋ")
aline(c("batu","kərampu"), c("batʊ","ləməntuŋ"))
aline("watu", "dat", sim = TRUE) 
ALINE.segments(raw.alignment(c("watu","dat"))) 
aline(c("batu","kərampu"), c("batʊ","ləməntuŋ"), Place = 10) 
aline(c("ũmlatʃ","dinnira"), c("omlatʃ","diŋŋira"))  
```


Working copy: `alineR/alineR/` (copied from the untouched CRAN source in
`alineR_archive/alineR_1.1.4/`). Each fix is checked with:

```text
R CMD build alineR
R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual alineR_<version>.tar.gz   # 1.1.4 until fix 3, then 1.1.5
```

### Issue list

| # | Problem | Source | Status |
|:--|:--------|:-------|:-------|
| 1 | C++ reads 13 feature weights from a 12-element vector | CRAN valgrind (cause of archival) | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 2 | Examples write `candidate_alignments.csv`, `open.with.excel.csv` into the working directory | CRAN NOTE (cause of archival) | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 3 | Version 1.1.4 equals the archived version | WARNING, CRAN incoming feasibility | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 4 | Two URLs moved (301): Kondrak homepage, R Journal article | NOTE, CRAN incoming feasibility (part of the WARNING before fix 3) | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 5 | Invalid package alias `aline-package` | NOTE, Rd metadata | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 6 | Template keywords `~kwd1`, `~kwd2` in `features.plot.Rd`, `optimization.GA.Rd` | NOTE, Rd contents | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 7 | C++ buffer overflow: words of ~12+ encoded characters give corrupted alignments; ~25+ crash R | Found locally (AddressSanitizer); not in CRAN checks | Fixed (2026-11-14) |
| 8 | Invalid input (empty word, word starting with a modifier, unknown code such as `@`, NA weights) reaches the C++ unchecked: out-of-bounds write (`phon[-1]`), integer overflow, silent garbage | Correctness check (UBSan) | Fixed (2026-11-14) |

### Step 0: baseline (2026-11-14)

Unmodified 1.1.4 on R 4.6.2, macOS: `Status: 1 WARNING, 3 NOTEs` (issues 2-6
above). Issue 1 does not show in a normal check; CRAN found it with valgrind.

Reference outputs (the worked examples in Downey, Sun & Norquest 2017), used
to confirm that fixes do not change results:

```text
aline("kərampu", "ləməntuŋ")                                      0.4864198
aline(c("batu","kərampu"), c("batʊ","ləməntuŋ"))                  0.0000000 0.4864198
aline("watu", "dat", sim = TRUE)                                  50
ALINE.segments(raw.alignment(c("watu","dat")))                    0 0 15 35
aline(c("batu","kərampu"), c("batʊ","ləməntuŋ"), Place = 10)      0.0000000 0.4567901
optimized weights 61 92 51 26 54 38 20 40 31 38 66 72 60          0.0000000 0.5604938
aline(c("ũmlatʃ","dinnira"), c("omlatʃ","diŋŋira"))               0.07647059 0.10810811
```

### Fix 1: out-of-bounds read in `src/alineR.cpp` (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** CRAN's valgrind run reported `Invalid read of size 4` at
`exchange (alineR.cpp:19)`. `raw.alignment()` passes 12 feature weights
(Syllabic ... Round), and the skip penalty separately. The C++ copied 13:

```cpp
int vec[13]; for(int i=0;i<13;i++) vec[i]=INTEGER(coeff)[i];
```

so it read one integer past the end of the R vector. The 13th value was never
used as a weight (feature indices run 0-11), so results were unaffected, but
reading outside the vector is undefined behaviour.

**Fix.** Read exactly 12 values and reject anything else:

```cpp
if (TYPEOF(coeff) != INTSXP || LENGTH(coeff) != 12)
    Rf_error("feature weights must be an integer vector of length 12");
int vec[12]; for(int i=0;i<12;i++) vec[i]=INTEGER(coeff)[i];
```

**GitHub:** [86c8a42](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/86c8a42738b6d59c228b92ddd2267d005c42141d) (diff against the [untouched baseline](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/dba2ff881c7829d9d971b1875e7828f63637c9e8)).

**Verified.** All reference outputs identical to step 0. Passing 13 weights now
gives an R error. `R CMD check` unchanged (`1 WARNING, 3 NOTEs`), as expected
since this bug only shows under valgrind. Final confirmation needs a valgrind
run (rhub `valgrind` platform), since valgrind is not available on macOS.

### Fix 2: examples write CSV files to the working directory (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** CRAN's check NOTE "non-standard things in the check directory"
listed `candidate_alignments.csv` and `open.with.excel.csv`. CRAN policy does
not allow writing to the user's file space unless asked. Two sources:

- `generate.training()` defaulted to `table = TRUE`, so the `optimize.features`
  example wrote `candidate_alignments.csv`, although its comment says "(not written)".
- The `generate.training` example wrote `open.with.excel.csv` to the working directory.

**Fix.** Default `table = FALSE` in `generate.training()` (code and Rd), and
write the example's CSV to `tempdir()`:

```r
generate.training <- function(raw.data, search.size = 1000, table = FALSE,
                              file.out = "candidate_alignments.csv")
```

```r
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "open.with.excel.csv")
M <- generate.training(raw.data = data, search.size = 100, table = TRUE, file.out = out)
```

**GitHub:** [1281733](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/128173394a0b89b07b99b3dd90badb7109c671e9)

**Verified.** `R CMD check`: `1 WARNING, 2 NOTEs` (was `1 WARNING, 3 NOTEs`);
"non-standard things in the check directory" now OK and no CSV files left in
the check directory. A default `generate.training()` call writes no files;
`table = TRUE` still writes `file.out`. Note: users who relied on the old
default must now pass `table = TRUE`.

### Fix 3: version equals the archived version (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** The CRAN incoming check gave a WARNING: "Insufficient package
version (submitted: 1.1.4, existing: 1.1.4)" and "The Date field is over a
month old". CRAN rejects a resubmission with an unchanged version.

**Fix.** Version 1.1.5 (patch release). In `DESCRIPTION`:

```text
Version: 1.1.5
Date: 2026-11-14
```

and removed the fields CRAN and `R CMD build` add themselves, which were stale
from 2017 (`Packaged`, `Repository`, `Date/Publication`). Also:

- Removed the CRAN-generated `MD5` file: it no longer matched the sources after
  fixes 1-2 (`tools::checkMD5sums()` was FALSE) and is regenerated on build.
- Updated the version/date in `man/aline-package.Rd` and the version in `inst/CITATION`.

The earlier, discarded fix attempt's git tag `alineR-1.1.5` and branch
`alineR-cran-1.1.5` were deleted so the name refers only to this release.

**GitHub:** [45cacfb](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/45cacfbe0fa50f307bb03d905dfebf6faa60b66a)

**Verified.** `R CMD check`: `0 WARNINGs, 3 NOTEs` (was `1 WARNING, 2 NOTEs`).
The incoming-feasibility check is now a NOTE: the expected "New submission /
Package was archived on CRAN" text, plus the moved URLs (issue 4).

### Fix 4: moved URLs (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** The CRAN incoming check listed two URLs answering
`301 Moved Permanently`: the R Journal article
(`https://journal.r-project.org/archive/2017/RJ-2017-005/index.html`, in
`DESCRIPTION`, `man/aline-package.Rd`, `inst/CITATION`) and Kondrak's homepage
(`http://webdocs.cs.ualberta.ca/~kondrak/`, in `man/aline-package.Rd`).

**Fix.**

- R Journal article: replaced by its DOI, `10.32614/RJ-2017-005`
  (`<doi:...>` in `DESCRIPTION`, `\doi{}` in Rd, `doi =` in `CITATION`).
  CRAN prefers DOIs, and DOIs are not flagged when the publisher moves pages.
- Kondrak's homepage now answers `410 Gone` with no successor, so the link is
  dropped; the acknowledgement stays.
- Same category, not flagged by CRAN: the 2008 reference had a malformed
  `doi://dx.doi.org/...` (now `\doi{10.1080/09296170802326681}`), and the
  `DESCRIPTION` text was missing a closing parenthesis.

**GitHub:** [6ddb544](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/6ddb544cc38d3ac00a1811598294f253dc7522cb)

**Verified.** `R CMD check`: `0 WARNINGs, 3 NOTEs`; the incoming NOTE no
longer lists URLs, only the expected "New submission / Package was archived on
CRAN". `citation("alineR")` and the package help page show working DOIs.

### Fix 5: invalid package alias (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** `R CMD check` NOTE (Rd metadata): "Invalid package aliases in Rd
file 'aline-package.Rd': 'aline-package'". The package overview page must have
the alias `<package>-package`, i.e. `alineR-package`.

**Fix.** In `man/aline-package.Rd`:

```text
\name{alineR-package}
\docType{package}
\alias{alineR-package}
\alias{alineR}
```

The extra `alineR` alias makes `?alineR` open the overview page.

**GitHub:** [97a7dc9](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/97a7dc90467dea62ccffadfe05df084e55eee35a)

**Verified.** `R CMD check`: `0 WARNINGs, 2 NOTEs` (was 3); "Rd metadata" OK.
`?"alineR-package"` and `?alineR` both resolve.

**Problem.** `R CMD check` NOTE (Rd contents): "Auto-generated content

### Fix 7: C++ buffer overflow on long words (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** Found locally with AddressSanitizer; CRAN never saw it because no
example uses a long word. Fixed-size C++ buffers did not fit each other:

| Buffer | Old size | Needed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| input copy (`alineR.cpp`) | `char s1[20]`, filled by `strcpy` | word length + 1 |
| alignment output | `char aback[50]` | 4 chars per aligned position |
| trace stack / DP matrix (`MAXL`) | 40 | `lenA + lenB + 2` |
| word representation (`ELEN`) | 30 | word length + 1 |

Words are measured after encoding (e.g. `ŋ` becomes `gN`). Probe aligning a
word with itself (`raw.alignment(c(w, w))`), unmodified code:

```text
n= 10  segments in alignment= 10  identical rows=TRUE      correct
n= 11  segments in alignment=  0  identical rows=FALSE     corrupted
n= 15  segments in alignment=  3  identical rows=FALSE     corrupted
n= 20  (R session crashed)
ASan:  stack-buffer-overflow in Stack::showAlign, from n = 11
```

Scores were not affected, only the alignment strings (and the crash).

**Fix.** One limit, every buffer derived from it (`src/glob.h`):

```cpp
const int ELEN = 61;              // max encoded word length + 1
const int PLEN = ELEN + 2;        // phonemic length
const int MAXL = 2 * ELEN + 4;    // alignment has <= lenA + lenB + 2 entries
const int ABACK = TAB * MAXL + 1; // output: <= TAB chars per entry
```

In `src/alineR.cpp` the words are no longer copied into `char[20]`; words of
more than 60 encoded characters raise an R error, and the output buffers are
`char[ABACK]`. Array parameters are declared `char *` instead of `char[50]`.

**GitHub:** [1176c73](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/1176c73055f40046cd5310bfd419698242050f46)

**Verified.**

- Probe: every length 8-60 aligns correctly (all segments present, identical
  rows); 61+ gives `word too long: at most 60 encoded characters are supported`.
- ASan/UBSan clean on the probe, on worst-case pairs (two unrelated 60-character
  words: 486 output chars, limit 505) and on 150 random pairs with skip penalties
  -100, 0, 100.
- Paper reference outputs identical to step 0. `R CMD check`: `1 NOTE` (unchanged).

### Correctness check, part 1 (2026-11-14)

After fixes 1-7, every exported function was compared between the original
1.1.4 and the fixed version, and run under AddressSanitizer/UBSan.

**Differential test** (1,500 random IPA word pairs of at most 10 encoded
characters, 1,500 random weight vectors, plus `encode.ALINE`, `decode.ALINE`,
`ALINE.segments`, custom mappings, `generate.training`, `optimize.features`,
`optimization.GA` with fixed seeds): all outputs identical, except 7 of the
1,500 weighted alignments. In those 7, 1.1.4 returned an empty `alignment1`:
alignments with many skips exceed the old 50-character output buffer even for
short words (issue 7). Structural check (each alignment row contains exactly
its word's letters): 1.1.4 valid 1,493/1,500, fixed version 1,500/1,500.

**Sanitizers.** All package examples clean. Malformed input found issue 8:
R compiles packages with `-DNDEBUG`, so the C++ `assert()` checks are disabled
and invalid words go through. UBSan: `index -1 out of bounds` (`Word.cpp:220`)
for an empty word or one starting with a modifier, e.g. `aline("ÈÈ", "ta")`
where all characters are unknown; `signed integer overflow` (`Word.cpp:292`)
for `NA` weights.

### Fix 8: invalid input reached the C++ unchecked (2026-11-14)

**Problem.** The C++ guards its input with `assert()`, but R compiles packages
with `-DNDEBUG`, so the checks never run. Under UBSan:

| Input | Example | 1.1.4 behaviour |
|:--|:--|:--|
| empty word | `aline("ÈÈ", "ta")` (all characters unknown, dropped) | write to `phon[-1]`, garbage result |
| word starting with a modifier or `@` | `raw.alignment(c("Nta","ta"))`, `aline("Èta","ta", mark = TRUE)` | write to `phon[-1]` |
| NA weight | `raw.alignment(c("ta","ta"), Place = NA)` | signed integer overflow |
| NA word | `raw.alignment(c(NA,"ta"))` | aligns the literal text `"NA"` |

All returned a value silently.

**Fix.** `exchange()` in `src/alineR.cpp` rejects exactly these cases with an
R error:

```text
word 1 is empty (were all of its characters invalid?)
word 1 must start with a known segment (encoded a-z), not 'N'
word 1 is NA
feature weights must not be NA
skip penalty must be a single non-missing number
```

Unknown codes after the first character remain ignored, as in 1.1.4. That is
how the `@` placeholder of `aline(mark = TRUE)` works, so it keeps working for
unknown characters inside a word.

**GitHub:** [b0298da](https://github.com/Guowei-Sun-Meta/alineR/commit/b0298da60158ef121575245f584332f1307ae65b)

**Verified.** UBSan/ASan clean on all malformed inputs and all examples.
Paper reference outputs and the full differential test (1,500 pairs, all
exported functions) identical to fix 7. `R CMD check`: `1 NOTE` (unchanged).

### Correctness check, part 2: final 1.1.5 (2026-11-14)

Fresh build of the final 1.1.5 (package identical to the state after fix 8).
All checks are in `checks/` and rerun with `bash checks/run_checks.sh` (macOS).

| Check | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `R CMD check --as-cran` (R 4.6.2, macOS) | `Status: 1 NOTE` (CRAN incoming: new submission / archived) |
| Paper worked examples (7) | identical to the published values |
| Differential test vs 1.1.4 (1,500 random pairs, all exported functions) | 11 of 12 output groups identical; weighted alignments: 1.1.5 valid 1,500/1,500, 1.1.4 valid 1,493/1,500 (issue 7) |
| ASan/UBSan: all examples, words of 8-100 encoded characters, worst-case pairs, 150 random pairs, malformed input | 0 sanitizer reports; too long, empty, NA and malformed words give R errors |

Not covered locally: valgrind (not available on macOS). Fix 1 is a read past
the end of an R vector inside R's own memory pool, which ASan cannot see; it is
verified by the length check in the code and should be confirmed with the R-hub
`valgrind` platform before submission (`SUBMISSION.md`, step 3). Not tested:
R-devel and Windows (win-builder, also step 3).
